dialogues.title: 校园初次见面 (First Meeting on Campus)
dialogues.scene: Two students introduce themselves at a Chinese university.

lines.speaker: 李明 (Lǐ Míng)
lines.ref: Hello! My name is Li Ming.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.ref: Hi, Li Ming! My name is Anna.

lines.speaker: 李明 (Lǐ Míng)
lines.ref: Anna, what country are you from?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.ref: I'm American. And you?

lines.speaker: 李明 (Lǐ Míng)
lines.target: 我是中国人。你为什么学中文?
lines.ref: I'm Chinese. Why are you studying Chinese?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.target: 因为我很喜欢中国文化。
lines.ref: Because I really like Chinese culture.

lines.speaker: 李明 (Lǐ Míng)
lines.ref: You speak Chinese very well!

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.ref: Thank you! Let's be friends.

lines.speaker: 李明 (Lǐ Míng)
lines.ref: Sure! Nice to meet you.

dialogues.note: When someone praises your Chinese with 说得很好, the polite Chinese reply is often modest — 哪里哪里 (nǎlǐ nǎlǐ, 'not at all') is a classic humble response.

dialogues.title: 在餐厅点菜 (Ordering at a Restaurant)
dialogues.scene: A customer orders dishes and asks about spice level.

lines.speaker: 服务员 (Server)
lines.ref: Welcome! How many people, please?

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: Two. Please give me the menu.

lines.speaker: 服务员 (Server)
lines.ref: Okay. What would you like to eat?

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: Is this Kung Pao chicken spicy?

lines.speaker: 服务员 (Server)
lines.target: 有一点辣。可以不放辣椒。
lines.ref: A little spicy. We can leave out the chili.

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.target: 好,我要一个宫保鸡丁和一碗米饭。
lines.ref: Okay, I'll have one Kung Pao chicken and a bowl of rice.

lines.speaker: 服务员 (Server)
lines.ref: Anything to drink?

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: Two cups of tea, thank you.

lines.speaker: 服务员 (Server)
lines.ref: Okay, please wait a moment.

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.target: 麻烦你,吃完帮我们买单。
lines.ref: Excuse me, please bring the bill when we're done.

dialogues.note: In China, calling out 服务员! to get the server's attention is normal and not rude. Tipping is generally not expected in mainland restaurants.

dialogues.title: 在北京打车 (Taking a Taxi in Beijing)
dialogues.scene: A passenger tells the driver the destination and chats.

lines.speaker: 司机 (Driver)
lines.ref: Hello, where to?

lines.speaker: 乘客 (Passenger)
lines.ref: Master (driver), I'm going to Tiananmen.

lines.speaker: 司机 (Driver)
lines.ref: Okay, fasten your seatbelt.

lines.speaker: 乘客 (Passenger)
lines.ref: About how much will it cost to get there?

lines.speaker: 司机 (Driver)
lines.target: 差不多五十块,看路上堵不堵。
lines.ref: Around fifty yuan, depending on the traffic.

lines.speaker: 乘客 (Passenger)
lines.ref: Is it very congested now?

lines.speaker: 司机 (Driver)
lines.target: 这个时间有点堵,可能要半个小时。
lines.ref: At this hour it's a bit jammed, it might take half an hour.

lines.speaker: 乘客 (Passenger)
lines.ref: No problem, I'm not in a hurry.

lines.speaker: 司机 (Driver)
lines.ref: All right, I'll let you know when we arrive.

lines.speaker: 乘客 (Passenger)
lines.target: 谢谢师傅,可以用手机付款吗?
lines.ref: Thanks, driver. Can I pay by phone?

lines.speaker: 司机 (Driver)
lines.ref: Sure, just scan this code.

dialogues.note: 师傅 (shīfu) is the respectful way to address a taxi driver, cook, or any skilled worker. Mobile payment via QR code is nearly universal in Chinese cities.

dialogues.title: 在市场砍价 (Bargaining at the Market)
dialogues.scene: A shopper haggles over a scarf and pays with WeChat.

lines.speaker: 老板 (Vendor)
lines.target: 看看吧,这条围巾很好看!
lines.ref: Take a look, this scarf is really pretty!

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: How much is this one?

lines.speaker: 老板 (Vendor)
lines.ref: One hundred eighty yuan.

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: Too expensive! Make it a bit cheaper.

lines.speaker: 老板 (Vendor)
lines.ref: Then how much do you want to offer?

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: How about one hundred yuan?

lines.speaker: 老板 (Vendor)
lines.ref: That's too low, let's say one hundred fifty.

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: A hundred twenty — if that works, I'll buy it.

lines.speaker: 老板 (Vendor)
lines.target: 好吧,交个朋友,一百二拿走。
lines.ref: Fine, for friendship's sake, one twenty and it's yours.

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.target: 我用微信付,给我看看二维码。
lines.ref: I'll pay by WeChat, show me the QR code.

lines.speaker: 老板 (Vendor)
lines.ref: Scan here, thanks for your business!

dialogues.note: Bargaining is expected at open markets but not in malls or supermarkets. Starting around half the asking price and settling in the middle is a common rhythm.

dialogues.title: 电话订酒店 (Booking a Hotel by Phone)
dialogues.scene: A traveler calls a hotel to reserve a room.

lines.speaker: 前台 (Front Desk)
lines.target: 您好,这里是阳光酒店,请问有什么可以帮您?
lines.ref: Hello, this is Sunshine Hotel, how may I help you?

lines.speaker: 客人 (Guest)
lines.ref: Hello, I'd like to book a room.

lines.speaker: 前台 (Front Desk)
lines.ref: How many nights will you be staying?

lines.speaker: 客人 (Guest)
lines.target: 从这周五到周日,一共两晚。
lines.ref: From this Friday to Sunday, two nights in total.

lines.speaker: 前台 (Front Desk)
lines.target: 您要单人间还是双人间?
lines.ref: Would you like a single or a double room?

lines.speaker: 客人 (Guest)
lines.target: 一个双人间,请问多少钱一晚?
lines.ref: A double room, how much is it per night?

lines.speaker: 前台 (Front Desk)
lines.target: 每晚三百八十块,含早餐。
lines.ref: Three hundred eighty yuan per night, breakfast included.

lines.speaker: 客人 (Guest)
lines.target: 可以要一个安静的房间吗?
lines.ref: Could I have a quiet room?

lines.speaker: 前台 (Front Desk)
lines.target: 没问题,我给您安排高层。
lines.ref: No problem, I'll arrange a room on a higher floor.

lines.speaker: 客人 (Guest)
lines.target: 太好了,我姓王,电话是139开头的。
lines.ref: Great, my surname is Wang, my number starts with 139.

lines.speaker: 前台 (Front Desk)
lines.target: 好的,王先生,已经为您预订好了。
lines.ref: Okay, Mr. Wang, your reservation is confirmed.

dialogues.note: Chinese hotels usually require you to leave a deposit (押金 yājīn) at check-in, refunded when you return the key card and settle the bill.

dialogues.title: 在药店看病 (At the Pharmacy)
dialogues.scene: A customer describes symptoms and asks for medicine.

lines.speaker: 药剂师 (Pharmacist)
lines.ref: Hello, what's bothering you?

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.target: 我从昨天开始头疼,还有一点发烧。
lines.ref: I've had a headache since yesterday, and a slight fever too.

lines.speaker: 药剂师 (Pharmacist)
lines.target: 有没有咳嗽或者嗓子疼?
lines.ref: Do you have a cough or a sore throat?

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.target: 嗓子有点疼,不怎么咳嗽。
lines.ref: My throat hurts a bit, but I'm not coughing much.

lines.speaker: 药剂师 (Pharmacist)
lines.target: 应该是感冒了。我给您拿点感冒药。
lines.ref: It's probably a cold. I'll get you some cold medicine.

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: How do I take this medicine?

lines.speaker: 药剂师 (Pharmacist)
lines.target: 一天三次,一次两片,饭后吃。
lines.ref: Three times a day, two tablets each time, after meals.

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: Can I drive after taking it?

lines.speaker: 药剂师 (Pharmacist)
lines.target: 最好别开,这个药会让人想睡觉。
lines.ref: Better not — this medicine can make you drowsy.

lines.speaker: 顾客 (Customer)
lines.ref: I understand. Drink plenty of water, right?

lines.speaker: 药剂师 (Pharmacist)
lines.target: 对,多喝水,多休息,很快就好了。
lines.ref: Yes, drink lots of water, rest well, and you'll recover soon.

dialogues.note: Chinese pharmacies (药店) often stock both Western medicine (西药) and traditional Chinese medicine (中药); staff may ask which you prefer for a common cold.
